question.problem: Find the derivative of  $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+3t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t\end{aligned}]$ at $t=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+3t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2t+3 \\ \frac{1}{t} \\ \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute ${f}^{′}(1)$ we substitute $t=1$ into the expression for ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =[\begin{aligned}2(1)+3 \\ \frac{1}{1} \\ \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2+3 \\ 1 \\ \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi \end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -\pi \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
